title: Permission Endpoint
description: The permission endpoint enables agents to request permission from the PS for actions **not governed by a remote resource** — tool calls, file writes, sending messages on behalf of the user. The spec says this MAY be used **with or without a mission** (§1015), and the without-mission case is the more important pitch: it lets the PS govern agent behavior **before any resources support AAuth**, giving users one chokepoint that sees every sensitive local action. The PS decides each request against its standing user policy and, if needed, defers to the user via the same `202 + AAuth-Requirement: interaction` pattern other AAuth endpoints use. Only `action` is required (§1025); `description`, `parameters`, and `mission` are optional. Toggle **With Mission** above to see how `approved_tools` (§1303) bypasses the endpoint entirely and how the request binds to a mission log.

steps.label: POST /permission (SendEmail) → 200 granted by standing policy

request_body.description: Email the draft Q2 wrap-up to the user's own address.

annotations: Agent signs the request with its agent token via Signature-Key: sig=jwt (§1021). No mission is bound — the request body has no `mission` field.
Only `action` is required (§1025). `description` and `parameters` are optional but recommended so the PS (and the user, if asked) can see what's being attempted.
Without a mission, the PS evaluates against the user's **standing policy** at the PS — "always allow SendEmail to my own domain" is a reasonable default.
PS decides immediately and returns 200 `permission: "granted"` (§1055, §1068). PS SHOULD still record the request even without a mission (§1075).

steps.label: POST /permission (PublishToSocial) → 202 (no policy match — defer to user)

request_body.description: Post a short summary of the Q2 highlights to the company LinkedIn page.

parameters.text: Q2 highlights — see thread for the top three themes…

annotations: No matching standing policy → the PS cannot decide alone and uses the standard deferred-response pattern (§1073).
Same `202 + AAuth-Requirement: interaction` shape the token endpoint uses for consent — the agent doesn't need a new state machine.
`Location` is the pending URL the agent polls; `url` + `code` in AAuth-Requirement point the user at the consent page (step 3).
Agent waits Retry-After seconds before polling.

steps.label: User opens interaction URL → consent page
steps.response_body:
Agent requests permission to perform an action

The agent aauth:local@agent.example is asking to perform:

  • action: PublishToSocial
  • channel: linkedin
  • preview: “Q2 highlights — see thread for the top three themes…”

You have no standing rule for this action. Allow it?
annotations: PS renders the consent page from the `code` in step 2's AAuth-Requirement header.
Without a mission, the "approve & remember" affordance is how users build up standing policy over time — next time PublishToSocial comes in, it'll be granted in step 1.
Clarification chat (§912) MAY happen here if the user wants to ask the agent why it needs this.

steps.label: GET /pending/p9c4e1a2 → 200 granted
annotations: Polling at the pending URL follows the same pattern as the token endpoint — signed GET with the agent's key.
Once the user approves at the consent page, the next poll returns the final `permission: "granted"` response (§1068).
Agent now SHOULD perform the action and MAY log it. Without a mission there's no mission log, but the PS may still keep its own audit trail of permission decisions (§1075).

steps.label: POST /permission (DeleteAllRecords) → 200 denied by standing policy

request_body.description: Clear the raw Q2 feedback table.

response_body.reason: Destructive bulk operations are blocked by your standing policy. The agent should ask for a narrower action, or you can lift this rule in PS settings.

annotations: PS can deny without bothering the user when standing policy explicitly forbids the action (§1069).
`reason` is a Markdown string the agent can surface to its user or log (§1069).
This is the value prop of the no-mission case: a single chokepoint where the user pre-declares "never let any agent do X" and the PS enforces it.

events.detail: Standing user policy allows email to own domain — PS decides alone

events.label: User reviews & approves
events.detail: Consent page rendered from the interaction code

events.label: Polled response: granted
events.detail: Pending URL now returns the final permission decision

events.detail: Standing policy forbids destructive bulk ops — denied with reason

interactive.description: The same three requests, this time inside a mission. Each names mission_s256, so the PS evaluates them against the approved description, the approved tool list and the mission log rather than against standing policy alone — and records each decision in that log.

mission_blob.title: Mission in force
mission_blob.description: The approved mission these permission requests are evaluated against.
mission_blob.markdown:
# Analyze Q2 Customer Feedback

Read customer feedback records and produce a summary report with sentiment analysis and key themes.

approved_tools.name: ReportWriter
approved_tools.description: Write the summary report to the shared drive

steps.label: POST /permission (SendEmail + mission) → 200 granted

request_body.description: Email the finished Q2 feedback summary to the user as an attachment.

annotations: mission_s256 is OPTIONAL on the permission endpoint. When present, the PS evaluates the request against the mission context and the log history.
SendEmail is on the mission's approved_tools list, so the PS decides immediately: 200 permission=granted.
Nothing in the protocol enforces approved_tools — it is what the person agreed to in advance, and the PS is free to ask anyway.
The PS records the request and the response in the mission log.

steps.label: POST /permission (PublishToSocial + mission) → 202 (user consent required)

request_body.description: Post a short summary of the Q2 feedback highlights to the company LinkedIn page.

parameters.text: Q2 customer feedback highlights — see thread for the top three themes…

annotations: Publishing externally is outside `approved_tools` AND outside the spirit of "analyze and report internally," so the PS cannot decide alone.
Standard deferred-response pattern (§1073) — same shape as the no-mission case.
User consent prompt may include an "add to approved_tools" affordance — but that produces a NEW s256 (mission supersession, see Out-of-Bounds demo).

steps.label: User opens interaction URL → consent page (mission context shown)
steps.response_body:
Agent requests permission to perform an action

The agent aauth:local@agent.example is operating under the mission Analyze Q2 Customer Feedback.

It is asking to perform:

  • action: PublishToSocial
  • channel: linkedin
  • preview: “Q2 customer feedback highlights — see thread for the top three themes…”

This action was not pre-approved when you accepted the mission. Allow it?
annotations: Same consent flow as the no-mission case — but the page surfaces the mission title so the user has full context.
"Add to approved_tools" extends the mission, which produces a NEW s256 (supersession). See Out-of-Bounds demo for that pattern.

steps.label: GET /pending/p9c4e1a2 → 200 granted
annotations: Polling pattern is identical to the no-mission case — same pending URL semantics.
Final response: `permission: "granted"`. The original request, the user's decision, and this response are all recorded in the mission log (§1075).
Agent SHOULD now perform the action and call /audit to log the outcome — see Audit Endpoint demo.

steps.label: POST /permission (DeleteAllRecords + mission) → 200 denied (out-of-scope)

request_body.description: Clear the raw Q2 feedback table after the report is published.

response_body.reason: Destructive operations on source data are outside this mission's scope. The mission authorized **read + summarize**, not **delete**. Propose a new mission if cleanup is required.

annotations: DeleteAllRecords is not on the approved tool list and standing policy forbids destructive bulk operations, so the PS denies without troubling the person.
reason is a Markdown string the agent can surface or log.
If the mission were no longer active, this would be 403 mission_terminated instead.
